gen-dafont-redux-gf-hind-madurai: Hind Madurai fills its lines with lowercase that stands nearly as tall as capitals, and its stroke ends look cut from one ribbon. Redux leads with a faint wire-like taper, but the sans below keeps horizontals as sturdy as verticals, so a long stretch of text moves along steadily.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-hind-mysuru: Redux spaces its letters wide and swoops into every curve with a visible entrance, giving the heading a geometric stride. And Hind Mysuru follows with sans lowercase pressed up toward the ascender line, its strokes like twine with no thinning, so the two sit together without fuss.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara draws its lines like sign-shop vinyl, one width throughout, with open rounded shapes and tall bowls in the a and e. Redux is best at showing off its slight rubber-cord weight shifts and wide spacing, while the sans simply does the quiet work of being clear.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-huninn: Redux stretches its letters wide and sweeps into each curve, with stems a touch heavier than its hairlines. Huninn counters with sans-serif lowercase that rises near cap height and crossbars as fat as their stems, and that sturdy sameness is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-inter-tight: Redux sets a generous letter spacing and a visible sweep into every curve, with strokes that thicken and thin in gentle steps. Inter Tight runs like bent tubing, plain and unswelling.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and friendly, its middle band so tall and its c so gaping that lines feel chunky and open. Redux adds a faint stone-carved heft to wide, geometric headings, and the lowness of the sans lets that character come through unchallenged.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-kedebideri: Wide, geometric and a little showy, Redux sweeps into each curve with moderate stroke contrast and big lowercase. Kedebideri answers with a sky-high x-height and low-contrast sans curves.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-khula: Redux is defined by its wide spacing and a big visible entrance into every curve, with the mild stroke variation of a gently used dip pen. Khula follows with a sans whose tall midsection feels like a squat brush-pen belly, and curves that hold their mouths open.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-krub: Redux lets its letters spread wide, entering each curve with a big visible sweep, and its stems run just a touch thicker than the strokes connecting them. But Krub keeps a plain sans manner underneath, its pronounced x-height and unfinished curve loops making a long page feel breezy.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-kufam: Redux spaces its enlarged lowercase wide and bends every curve in with a visible entrance, its gentle modulation keeping paragraphs comfortable. Kufam is the plain sans, drawn like neon tube.
